q_45367.question_text: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)
q_45367.reasoning:
Let me work through this systematically.

## (a) Time left until resolution

Today is August 20, 2026. NVIDIA's Q2 FY2027 earnings release is stated to occur on August 26, 2026 in the research summary. This means resolution is **6 days away**.

## (b) Most likely outcome and why

NVIDIA has already issued forward guidance for Q2 FY2027 on May 20, 2026, predicting revenue of **$91.0 billion ± 2%** (so a range of $89.18B to $92.82B). 

With the earnings release just 6 days away, the guidance is almost certainly already set and locked in. Companies rarely change their forward guidance in the final week before an earnings call. The research indicates:
- NVIDIA's prior guidance: $91.0B ± 2%
- Current analyst consensus for Q2 FY2027: ~$91.85B
- The range provided is 99.5B to 115.5B (lower and upper bounds open)

The most likely scenario is that NVIDIA will reaffirm or slightly adjust their $91.0B guidance, with final guidance landing somewhere in the $89B-$93B range.

## (c) What would push the value lower?

- Significant deterioration in AI/data center demand between May and August 2026
- Worse-than-expected Q1 FY2027 actual results (which would inform Q2 guidance)
- Geopolitical or regulatory impacts affecting China revenue exclusions
- Supply chain disruptions
- Macro economic deterioration

## (d) What would push the value higher?

- Stronger-than-expected actual results in Q1 FY2027
- Better AI adoption and demand trajectory than anticipated in May
- Competitive wins or new customer acquisitions
- Relaxation of China export restrictions (allowing inclusion of China revenue)
- Upside from data center utilization rates

## (e) Base rate or historical reference values

The research explicitly provides NVIDIA's own May 20, 2026 guidance: **$91.0 billion ± 2%** for Q2 FY2027. This is the most directly relevant "base rate" - it's NVIDIA's own forward estimate made just a few months prior to the August 26 earnings call. Current analyst consensus is around $91.85B.

With only 6 days to the earnings call, this guidance should be nearly final. Companies have strong incentives to under-promise and over-deliver, but major revisions at the last minute are rare.

## Reasoning on the range

The provided range is 99.5B to 115.5B, which is substantially higher than NVIDIA's current guidance of $91.0B ± 2%. This seems to reflect potential upside scenarios or perhaps uncertainty about what guidance NVIDIA might provide. However, with actual guidance already publicly issued at $91.0B just 3 months ago, and only 6 days until the official announcement, the most probable outcome clusters tightly around that $91.0B figure with modest adjustments.

I estimate:
- ~85% probability guidance falls in the $88.5B-$93.5B range (around the May guidance ± ~2.5%)
- ~10% probability of more significant upside (higher than $93.5B, possibly $95B-$100B range)
- ~5% probability of downside revision (below $88.5B)

The median expectation should be very close to the May guidance of $91.0B, with modest upward bias reflecting analyst consensus at $91.85B.

q_45367.research_text:
I found one contradiction:

The research summary states that NVIDIA's guidance issued on May 20, 2026, predicted Q2 FY2027 revenue of $91.0 billion. However, it also states that this guidance "was slightly below the LSEG average quarterly revenue estimate of $86.84 billion at the time."

$91.0 billion is not below $86.84 billion—it is above it. This is an internal contradiction regarding the relationship between the two figures.

Here is the corrected version:

NVIDIA's Q2 FY2027 earnings release on August 26, 2026, will include forward guidance for Q3 FY2027 revenue. Analysts' consensus revenue for Q3 FY2027 is currently $103.1 billion [rexshares.com](https://www.rexshares.com/nvidia-earnings/).

For the upcoming Q2 FY2027 report, NVIDIA's own guidance, issued on May 20, 2026, predicted revenue of $91.0 billion, plus or minus 2%, explicitly excluding any Data Center compute revenue from China [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm), [cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/20/nvidia-nvda-earnings-report-q1-2027.html), [ifyouspent.com](https://news.ifyouspent.com/en/news/nvidia-earnings-what-to-watch-august-2026/). Current analyst consensus for Q2 FY2027 revenue is around $91.85 billion [rexshares.com](https://www.rexshares.com/nvidia-earnings/), [ifyouspent.com](https://news.ifyouspent.com/en/news/nvidia-earnings-what-to-watch-august-2026/).

A key factor to watch in the Q3 FY2027 guidance is whether the exclusion of China Data Center compute revenue remains [rexshares.com](https://www.rexshares.com/nvidia-earnings/), [ifyouspent.com](https://news.ifyouspent.com/en/news/nvidia-earnings-what-to-watch-august-2026/).

Note: discarded the reference to LSEG's $86.84 billion estimate being higher than NVIDIA's $91.0 billion guidance, as this comparison is mathematically contradictory.
